name: Betawi

ancestors.notes: Malay lexifier: Betawi is a Malay-derived creoloid that formed among the mixed population of colonial-era Batavia; the bulk of its vocabulary and grammar continues Low Malay (Grijns 1991, Jakarta Malay: Its History and Its Kinship with Malay Dialects).

Javanese substrate: migrants from Central/East Java were a major component of Batavia's mixed founder population and contributed vocabulary and phonological features to Betawi (Ikranagara 1980, Muysken & Grijns literature on Jakarta Malay/Betawi genesis).
Sundanese substrate: West Javanese (Sundanese-speaking) population contact around Batavia, cited alongside Javanese in the standard Betawi-formation accounts (Grijns 1991).
Dutch adstrate: three centuries of Batavia/Jakarta colonial administration (VOC then Dutch East Indies) left loanwords in Betawi vocabulary.

Hokkien (Min Nan) adstrate: the Chinese-Indonesian (peranakan) community of colonial Batavia was predominantly Hokkien-speaking, and its long trade/urban contact contributed a lexical loan layer to Betawi (kongsi, cukong, toke-type peranakan borrowings); the influence is lexical rather than structural, so adstrate rather than substrate (Grijns 1991, Jakarta Malay; Ikranagara 1980).

notes: Betawi (Betawi Malay / basa Betawi) — Malayic (Austronesian) creole-influenced language of Jakarta, Indonesia. Written in the Latin script following Indonesian orthographic conventions. GRAPHEME INVENTORY NOT YET SPECIFIED: Betawi has no codified standard orthography of its own and its phonology is not documented to a level that supports a reliable letter→phoneme table here. ANCESTRY: Malay (ms) lexifier with Javanese (jv)/Sundanese (su) substrate influence, a Dutch (nl) adstrate loanword layer, and a Hokkien/Min Nan (nan) adstrate from the peranakan Chinese-Indonesian community of colonial Batavia, per Grijns (1991) and Ikranagara (1980).
